references.text: Matthew's parallel account of Jesus speaking to large crowds in parables. Jesus went out and sat by the sea, and great crowds gathered around him, and he spoke to them in parables.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus began teaching by the sea, a large crowd gathered, and he taught them many things in parables.
The immediate context: Jesus traveled from city to city and from village to village, preaching the gospel of God's kingdom, which explains why people from every town came to him.
Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he did not speak to them. This highlights Jesus' use of parables as a teaching method for large crowds.
Mark confirms that Jesus spoke the word to them in many such parables, as much as they could understand, and without a parable he did not speak to them.
A previous event in Luke where the crowd pressed in on Jesus to hear God's word, showing the same pattern of large crowds gathering around him.
Also in Luke, thousands of people gathered around Jesus, so many that they stepped on one another. This shows the repeated pattern of large crowds seeking him out.

Jesus explains why he speaks in parables: because it has been given to the disciples to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but not to the crowd. This provides theological background for Jesus' use of parables.
